name: Quy Nhon food guide
summary: Start with bún chả cá on Nguyễn Huệ: fried and steamed fish cake in a gently sweet fish-bone broth, with Binh Dinh's own chili sauce. After dark, the thin shrimp pancake waits on Diên Hồng and Đống Đa, and snails and grilled snacks fill the night streets.
body: The pancake is bánh xèo tôm nhảy, a thin yellow batter with small shrimp that turn red in the pan, wrapped with sprouts, cucumber, and sour star fruit. Some cooks use freshwater shrimp and others tôm đất from the Thị Nại lagoon. Go on a cool evening, when the menu also runs to squid, beef, and egg.

Mornings are bánh hỏi lòng heo, the Diêu Trì plate of fine rice strands, pork intestine, and hot porridge, or hủ tiếu mì hoành thánh on Ngô Thời Nhiệm. Bún nem and the bánh mì lagu pork soup in a lane off Nguyễn Huệ fill the middle of the day. At night, Phan Bội Châu and Ngô Văn Sở are the snack streets, snails go to Tăng Bạt Hổ, Mai Xuân Thưởng, and Đào Duy Từ, and seafood dinners go to Xuân Diệu and the Quy Nhơn–Nhơn Hội bridge.
Rượu Bàu Đá, the rice spirit from Cù Lâm in An Nhơn, is stronger than 50 degrees and poured with the seafood on Hòn Khô.
specialtiesLead: Twenty-one plates are eaten in Quy Nhon itself. Nine more belong to other Binh Dinh towns, and the town is on each row.
seoTitle: Quy Nhon food — bun cha ca, banh xeo, banh hoi
seoDescription: Quy Nhon food: bún chả cá on Nguyễn Huệ, bánh xèo tôm nhảy on Diên Hồng, bánh hỏi lòng heo at breakfast, and snails on the night streets.

sections.heading: Quy Nhon specialties
paragraphs: These are the plates of the city and its streets. Some kitchens put dill in the fish cake and some leave it out. The pancake shrimp are freshwater in some kitchens and tôm đất from the Thị Nại lagoon in others.

spots.name: Bun cha ca
spots.note: Fish cake in a broth of fish bone and fish head, usually tuna or sailfish rather than pork, with a chili sauce particular to Binh Dinh. The broth is gently sweet and not fishy, and fried and steamed cakes share the bowl.

spots.name: Cha ca
spots.note: Quy Nhon's tuna fish cake, fried until chewy and crisp or steamed with a thin yellow egg layer. It is the same cake that goes into bún chả cá.

spots.name: Banh hoi long heo
spots.note: A morning plate from Diêu Trì: rice strands finer than bún, with sliced pork intestine and pork, a bowl of hot porridge, and a slightly sweet garlic-chili fish sauce.

spots.name: Banh it la gai
spots.note: A glossy black cone of ramie leaf and sticky-rice flour around mung bean, dried coconut, and ginger. Expect a little bitterness from the leaf, sugar sweetness, and a chewy skin that does not stick to the teeth.

spots.name: Chao bo
spots.note: Beef porridge on a beef-bone broth, full of tendon, bone, and offal, with scallion and sawtooth herb. The broth is rich, fragrant, and slightly hot from the herbs.

spots.name: Goi bo
spots.note: A beef salad served beside cháo bò, Quy Nhon's beef porridge.

spots.name: Bun rieu cua
spots.note: Crab noodle soup: the crab is pounded, mixed with egg, and set into brown-gold sheets you can break with chopsticks, with seaweed in the pot. A full herb plate comes alongside.

spots.name: Goi ca chich
spots.note: A small freshwater fish, fried whole and rolled in a phở sheet with herbs and cucumber, or served raw as a salad once the bones are out.

spots.name: Chao cau gai
spots.note: Sea-urchin porridge made only with fresh urchin: the meat and roe are seasoned, stir-fried, and poured into boiling rice.

spots.name: Banh xeo tom nhay
spots.address: Diên Hồng and Đống Đa; Mỹ Cang, Tuy Phước
spots.note: A thin yellow pancake with small shrimp that turn red in the pan, bean sprouts, and scallion, crisp on the underside. Some cooks use freshwater shrimp, others tôm đất from the Thị Nại lagoon.

spots.name: Bun nem
spots.note: Fresh noodles with nem chua, grilled fish cake, herbs, peanut, pickled mustard, and coriander. The sauce balances sour, hot, salty, and sweet, and each shop keeps its own.

spots.name: Banh mi lagu
spots.note: A thick, glossy pork soup with a large piece of fragrant, tender pork, eaten hot with bread.

spots.name: Hu tieu mi hoanh thanh
spots.note: A breakfast bowl that brings hủ tiếu, mì, and hoành thánh wontons together, served on Ngô Thời Nhiệm by a Hoa family shop nearly 50 years old.

spots.name: Banh beo
spots.address: Nguyễn Tất Thành nối dài, Nguyễn Thái Học, and Mai Xuân Thưởng
spots.note: Bánh bèo is the cheap cake younger visitors eat in Quy Nhon, on Nguyễn Tất Thành nối dài, Nguyễn Thái Học, and Mai Xuân Thưởng.

spots.name: Nem nuong
spots.address: Phan Bội Châu and Ngô Văn Sở
spots.note: Nem nướng is a night snack on Phan Bội Châu and Ngô Văn Sở, eaten as walking food. It is a different plate from nem chợ huyện.

spots.name: Banh trang trung
spots.address: Phan Bội Châu and Ngô Văn Sở
spots.note: Bánh tráng trứng, rice paper with egg, is a night snack on Phan Bội Châu and Ngô Văn Sở.

spots.name: Banh canh
spots.address: Phan Bội Châu and Ngô Văn Sở
spots.note: Bánh canh is one of the night bowls on Phan Bội Châu and Ngô Văn Sở.

spots.name: Ca muc kho nuong
spots.address: Phan Bội Châu and Ngô Văn Sở
spots.note: Grilled dried fish and squid, a night snack on Phan Bội Châu and Ngô Văn Sở.

spots.name: Oc
spots.address: Tăng Bạt Hổ, Mai Xuân Thưởng, and Đào Duy Từ
spots.note: Snails of many kinds, eaten at low tables on Tăng Bạt Hổ, Mai Xuân Thưởng, and Đào Duy Từ at night.

spots.name: Rong bien
spots.note: Seaweed from the Bãi Xếp fishing village, dried for a cool summer drink or cooked into chè.

spots.name: Ruou Bau Da
spots.address: Cù Lâm, Nhơn Lộc, An Nhơn; with seafood at Hòn Khô
spots.note: A rice spirit stronger than 50 degrees from Cù Lâm in An Nhơn: clear, hot, and sharp, then sweet in the throat. On Hòn Khô it is poured with the island seafood.

sections.heading: Elsewhere in Binh Dinh
paragraphs: These belong to towns across Binh Dinh, from An Nhơn and Tuy Phước to Tây Sơn, Phù Mỹ, and Hoài Nhơn. Eat them where they are made, on a day out of the city.

spots.name: Nem cho huyen
spots.note: Fermented pork from Tuy Phước, chewy, nubbly, sour, and crisp with a clean sweetness. It is less soft than nem Thủ Đức and less sweet than nem Lai Vung or nem An Cựu.

spots.name: Bun song than
spots.note: Mung-bean noodles from An Thái, named for the strands pulled in pairs, cooked with shrimp or lean pork. In An Thái the bowl comes with chicken offal.

spots.name: Banh trang nuoc dua
spots.note: A Tam Quan rice cracker with coconut milk in the batter, eaten grilled and fragrant and rich from the coconut.

spots.name: Chim mia
spots.note: A small bird of the Tây Sơn cane fields, the color of a dry leaf, eaten in late winter and early spring. It is grilled over charcoal with pepper-lime salt or fried in peanut oil with toasted sesame.

spots.name: Bun tom Chau Truc
spots.note: Shrimp noodles from Châu Trúc: live shrimp from the Trà Ổ lagoon pounded and stirred into boiling noodle water, with scallion, coriander, and pepper. A grilled rice cracker comes on the side.

spots.name: Mam nhum
spots.note: Black sea urchin fermented in salt for 10 to 15 days into a smooth, thick, cloudy-red paste, salty, sour, and sweet with garlic and peppercorns. It was once sent to the king, and families often keep it rather than sell it.

spots.name: Cua huynh de
spots.note: The yellow, heavily spined crab of Tam Quan and Đề Gi, scarce and called the king of crabs, in season from lunar month 12 to lunar month 3. Steamed, it keeps its sweetness and the roe is rich.

spots.name: Gie bo
spots.note: A Bahnar beef broth from the An Khê and Vĩnh Thạnh highlands, now eaten in Tây Sơn, made with fresh small intestine and soured with lá giang. Chili, ginger, and lemongrass go in, and a few drops of bile add the bitterness locals look for.

spots.name: Banh uot Hoai Nhon
spots.note: Thin steamed rice sheets from Hoài Nhơn, stacked in layers and rolled with oil, fried scallion, and a sweet-sour fish sauce.

sections.heading: Streets
paragraphs: Quy Nhon eats by street. The night snack streets also sell kem ly, kem trộn, and sinh tố.

spots.name: Xuan Dieu
spots.note: Evening seafood on the beach road, with more tables near the Quy Nhơn–Nhơn Hội bridge.

spots.name: Dien Hong and Dong Da
spots.note: The streets for bánh xèo tôm nhảy on a cool evening.

spots.name: Phan Boi Chau and Ngo Van So
spots.nameVi: Phan Bội Châu and Ngô Văn Sở
spots.address: Phan Bội Châu and Ngô Văn Sở
spots.note: The night snack streets: nem nướng, bánh tráng trứng, bánh canh, bánh xèo, kem ly, kem trộn, sinh tố, and cá mực khô nướng. Numbers 185–187 Phan Bội Châu are the tourism office, not a stall.

spots.name: Snail streets
spots.nameVi: Tăng Bạt Hổ, Mai Xuân Thưởng, Đào Duy Từ
spots.address: Tăng Bạt Hổ, Mai Xuân Thưởng, and Đào Duy Từ
spots.note: Snails of many kinds, at low tables after dark.

spots.name: Nguyen Hue
spots.note: Bún chả cá on the street, bánh mì lagu in a lane off it, and seafood in the evening. Number 26 is the museum.

spots.name: Night market
spots.note: A food corner inside Nhà Văn hóa Lao động tỉnh, beside a walking street of clothes and souvenirs.

sections.heading: Breakfast
paragraphs: Breakfast is bánh hỏi lòng heo, the Diêu Trì plate with hot porridge, or hủ tiếu mì hoành thánh on Ngô Thời Nhiệm. Bún chả cá on Nguyễn Huệ is the other morning bowl.
